hiring_bar_summary.text: Two bars in sequence: an eligibility bar (U.S. Person / export-control / clearance eligibility on many roles, applied at application stage) and then a fairly conventional but mission-probing technical bar (coding incl. C++ debugging reports, design, and repeated 'why Anduril' motivation checks in candidate reports). Candidates who cannot clear the first bar should not spend prep time on the second.

screening_signals.claim: U.S. Person status is an explicit requirement on sourced SWE postings 'due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities'
Many roles require eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance (Secret on one sourced posting; Top Secret SCI on the scientific SWE posting, active TS/SCI listed as desired there)

The application asks directly whether the candidate will require sponsorship now or in the future (e.g. H-1B) - combined with export-control rules, non-U.S.-Persons should assume most SWE roles are closed and verify role-by-role
Transcripts are requested early in the application process on sourced postings to assess coursework fit (redaction of non-technical info permitted; unofficial transcripts acceptable)
Applications disclose third-party pre-employment risk/integrity screening (sanctions/watchlist/adverse-media checks) as part of the process
Mission motivation is a repeated interview theme in candidate reports ('why Anduril' asked across rounds) - anecdotal but consistent

red_flags: ELIGIBILITY FIRST: if you are not a U.S. Person, or would need H-1B sponsorship, most Anduril SWE roles are closed by export-control law - the application asks both questions directly. Do not advise anyone to misstate this (Doc 3 s3.2: never fabricate).
Clearance timelines are outside the candidate's control and can extend offers by months - plan finances/timing accordingly (general reported norm, labeled).
Onsite intensity: at least some postings require 5-days-per-week onsite presence - confirm per role.
Defence work itself is a values decision for the candidate: some strong engineers opt out; surface this neutrally and early.
thesis_text: Bottom line: at Anduril the first screen is legal, not technical - many SWE roles require U.S. Person status for export-controlled work and eligibility for a U.S. security clearance, and the application asks about both plus future sponsorship up front. If you clear eligibility, the technical bar reported by candidates is recognisably standard (coding screen, practical/C++ work, design, behavioural) with an unusually persistent motivation question: why defence, why Anduril. Who gets in: no public cohort data exists, so no school or feeder percentages can be honestly quoted; sourced postings name CS/engineering/math/physics backgrounds, C++/Python depth, and - distinctively - request transcripts early to check coursework fit. Stated vs revealed: postings state a speed-and-deployment culture (production systems over papers, small teams); the revealed filter is eligibility plus mission commitment. Routes in, ranked for an eligible candidate: (1) direct Greenhouse application to a posting matched to your systems/C++ evidence; (2) recruiter/referral route with the same evidence; (3) adjacent defence/autonomy/robotics experience first, then lateral. For a non-U.S.-Person the honest route ranking is: none at Anduril for export-controlled roles - redirect effort to non-defence employers and say so plainly. Gap to close: C++ fluency and a maths/estimation or systems project, plus a credible, specific mission answer. Plan: 30 days - eligibility self-check and C++ project; semester - autonomy/systems coursework or project; year - apply with transcript ready. Coffee chats: engineers on Lattice/autonomy teams; ask how clearance timelines affected their start dates. Risks/alternatives: clearance delays; values fit with defence work is the candidate's own call. Offer to execute: eligibility-checked target list, resume tailoring, outreach drafts.

section_confidence.screening_signals: sourced-qualitative (official application + official postings) - the strongest-sourced section in this record

known_biases_of_data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Anduril-specific: posting mirrors may lag Greenhouse; clearance/U.S.-Person requirements vary BY ROLE - some roles list Secret eligibility, others TS/SCI, and non-controlled roles may differ, so per-posting verification is mandatory.
